ed: Quick follow-up from yesterday's kernel RFC review — we need a concrete ops/playbook for running Triton and CUTLASS kernels side-by-side in the runtime. Short thread to capture owners and next steps.

sasha: +1. main pain points I heard: compatibility matrix, decision surface (when to pick trig vs cutlass), and rollout testing harness.

neel: Agreed. Also need a deterministic perf signal we can query during CI (not just ad-hoc bench runs).

ed: Proposed pragmatic rule: runtime exposes `kernel_preference` that maps to a tiny decision function: seq_len cutoff, batch_size cutoff, and HW capability flags. Default order: Triton optimized -> CUTLASS fallback -> reference CUDA kernel.

cara: Can we avoid shipping model-specific knobs? Ops want global policy + per-model overrides.

sasha: Yes: global policy lives in runtime config; model manifest can optionally include `kernel_hint` for corner cases. Hints won't override safety checks (e.g., if hardware lacks required ISA).

neel: Actionable items I suggest: 1) define the capability detection probe (vendor, SM arch, cupti flags), 2) implement a lightweight decision API `choose_kernel(seq_len,batch,hw_caps)` and make it pluggable, 3) add nightly perf job to register matrix. I'll own 1 & 2.

ed: Good. Sasha, can you own the nightly perf matrix and storage (time series + artifacts)? We need easy diffs between Triton builds and CUTLASS builds.

sasha: I got it. Plan: run bench matrix across seq_len=[16,64,512,1024], batch=[1,2,8,32], model shapes=[gpt2-ish, llama-ish], and collect p99+p50 latency and tokens/sec. Output JSON artifacts to s3 path `s3://redwood-kernel-bench/{date}/`.

cara: For rollouts: require canary policy that validates throughput and correctness on a small customer trace. If correctness differs, auto-fallback to safe CUDA kernel. Who builds the correctness harness?

sasha: I'll slip in a differential test that runs model outputs on both kernels for a curated prompt set and compares logits/tokens with tolerance. Will add as a gating step for canary.

ed: Needs an oncall handover doc. @cara can you add steps to the runtime oncall playbook: how to force a kernel switch, how to read the decision logs, and how to revert?

cara: Yep. Will add a section: `runtime kernel: emergency actions` with commands like:
```
# force kernel for model id
redwoodctl runtime set-kernel --model MODEL_ID --kernel cutlass--force
# view decision reason
redwoodctl runtime kernel-reason --request-id 1234
```
Also instructions to flip `kernel_preference` in config and trigger rolling restart.

neel: Small ops note: we should tag kernel builds with a `kernel_tag` emitted by CI (e.g., `triton-2026-03-xx`) and publish supported tag list to the capability probe so runtime logs the tag used. That makes debugging easier.

sasha: Will add kernel_tag to bench artifacts. Also will include binary hash and compiler flags.

ed: Security/compliance: private deployments might not permit Triton due to licensing or custom toolchain. Ensure runtime capability probe can be disabled and manifests can mark `allowed_kernels: [cutlass]`.

neel: We'll implement a `kernel_whitelist` at deployment-time; runtime will refuse to auto-select unlisted backends.

cara: Ops checklist items (short):
- Add `kernel_preference` config schema entry (prod+staging).
- Add `kernel_reasons` structured logs (kernel, reason, seq_len, batch).
- Expose per-request header `X-Redwood-Kernel` for debugging.
- Canary gating: throughput + correctness threshold.

ed: Timelines? Neel/Neel for probe & API: 2 weeks. Sasha for nightly bench harness + diff pages: 3 weeks. Cara for oncall/playbook + config schema: 1 week. I'll coordinate documentation and RFC update.

sasha: One more: we should capture cost signal too (tokens/sec * GPU unit cost) so recommendations consider economics. I'll add cost compute to bench outputs.

neel: For the `choose_kernel` API, I'll include a plugin hook so we can add ML-based selector later. Keep initial impl rule-based.

cara: I'll add quick runbook snippet to ops-docs and ping #eng-oncall when done.

ed: Thanks all. Final checklist (owner tags):
- capability probe + choose_kernel API -> neel
- nightly bench matrix & diffs + cost calc -> sasha
- oncall playbook + config schema + emergency commands -> cara
- update RFC with decisions and sample manifest fields -> ed

oncall-bot: Deploy scheduled: runtime-config change window 2026-04-02T02:00Z -> 2026-04-02T04:00Z. Reminder will be sent 24h prior.

ed: I'll PR the RFC update tomorrow and link the bench dashboard when available. @sasha @neel @cara flag if timeline needs shifting. :thumbsup:
